newsitem.title: GERMANY: Karadzic set for trial under conditions - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Karadzic set for trial under conditions - newspaper.

text.p: Former Bosnian Serb president Radovan Karadzic would accept a trial supervised by the U.N. war crimes tribunal if deemed necessary by his national judiciary, a German newspaper said on Wednesday.

In an advance summary of an interview with Karadzic to be published by the Sueddeutsche Zeitung on Friday, Karadzic, an indicted war criminal, is quoted as suggesting that his case be initially handed back to legal authorities in Bosnia.

"If the authorities in my country accuse me of a punishable offence, I am ready to answer in front of a court. I would submit myself to a trial supervised by the Hague tribunal and the international community," he was further quoted by the Munich daily as saying.

Karadzic, the post-war leadership in Bosnia's Serb republic as well as most ordinary Bosnian Serbs say he and indicted associates committed no war crimes against Moslems and Croats during the 1992-95 conflict.

Western analysts say the local Serb judiciary would be unlikely to approve putting Karadzic on trial since it is largely controlled by the ruling nationalist party, which he once led and still influences behind the scenes.
Karadzic's former army commander, General Ratko Mladic, is also wanted for trial by the U.N. tribunal in the Netherlands.
The Bosnian Serbs' wartime president is rarely seen in public but his heavily-armed guards are a fixture in Pale, the town where he maintains his headquarters just outside Sarajevo.

Although Western countries have frequently demanded his capture and extradition, no attempt has so far been made to arrest him by NATO peace troops in Bosnia, partly because of the risk of casualties.
